prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2026-05-28, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2026-05-28):
Fiscal period 2026 Q1 (filed 2026-05-28). Revenue 23,078M, gross margin 33%, operating income 2,554M (operating margin 11%), net income 1,628M, diluted EPS 2.9. Total assets 54,941M, total liabilities 64,211M, shareholders' equity -9,270M. Current assets 22,162M vs current liabilities 20,274M (current ratio 1.09), retained earnings -9,884M.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The reported balance sheet shows negative shareholders' equity and retained earnings, with total liabilities materially exceeding total assets. This capital-structure insolvency, combined with only modest operating-profit coverage of interest, places the issuer in the lower end of the "currently vulnerable" category under conventional rating definitions. Positive but not robust operating cash generation and a current ratio barely above 1.0 preclude an upgrade into B territory while still avoiding an outright "default imminent" label such as CC or C.
DECISION: CCC
